$comment: Manifest for Invoke-Deploy.ps1. runAs32Bit is FALSE on every package - that is the
single most important setting here. The Intune portal defaults to 32-bit, and a 32-bit
PowerShell host on 64-bit Windows hits WOW64 registry redirection, so the native
Uninstall hive and several net cmdlets return wrong or empty data. The fingerprint
still renders; it is just quietly incorrect.
Assignment is deliberately NOT automated - see Invoke-Deploy.ps1 header.

packages.name: Network Triage - Fingerprint (SYSTEM)
packages.description: Collects Wi-Fi/TCP/driver/filter fingerprint, runs bounded single vs parallel throughput probe, emits a VERDICT. Detection-only: exit 1 means an actionable verdict was reached.
packages.notes: Start here. Assign to a pilot group containing one KNOWN-GOOD device first to capture a baseline.

packages.name: Network Triage - Fingerprint (USER)
packages.description: User-context companion probe. Exposes per-user proxy/AV differences that SYSTEM cannot see. Diagnostic only, always exits 0.
packages.notes: Deploy only when the SYSTEM probe reports HEALTHY against a live user complaint.

packages.name: Network Fix - TCP Autotuning
packages.description: Restores normal TCP receive-window auto-tuning. Least disruptive fix in the kit: no reboot, no adapter bounce.
packages.notes: Safe to run fleet-wide on a schedule.

packages.name: Network Fix - Settings Reset
packages.description: Resets the Wi-Fi adapter's advanced properties to their driver defaults in a single adapter bounce. Reports static IP/DNS, WinHTTP proxy and persistent routes without changing them.
packages.notes: ORDER MATTERS: run this BEFORE Wi-Fi Power Management. Driver defaults include power saving, so this undoes that pair. Bounces the adapter (few seconds offline); 24-hour per-device cooldown.

packages.name: Network Fix - Wi-Fi Power Management
packages.description: Disables radio power-down and sets the wireless power plan to maximum performance.
packages.notes: May bounce the adapter (few seconds offline) IF selective suspend is wrong. Other changes apply live.

packages.name: Network Fix - Bandwidth Managers
packages.description: Uninstalls allowlisted OEM bandwidth managers (SmartByte, Killer suite). Reports but never removes Dell Optimizer / SupportAssist.
packages.notes: Run detection alone first - it doubles as the dry run and prints exactly what would be removed.

packages.name: Network Fix - WLAN Profile Refresh
packages.description: Refreshes the active WLAN profile in place and prunes stale non-active profiles. Never deletes the profile carrying the connection.
packages.notes: Refresh-in-place by design: delete-then-recreate can strand a remote device with no Wi-Fi.

packages.name: Network Audit - Filter Drivers
packages.description: Reports non-baseline NDIS bindings, third-party Winsock LSPs, and running inline inspection services. Detection-only, always exits 0.
packages.notes: Intentionally has no remediation - auto-unbinding a filter driver can sever connectivity.

packages.name: Network Fix - Wi-Fi Driver Update
packages.description: Applies Dell network-category driver updates only, via dcu-cli, with reboot suppressed.
packages.notes: Requires Dell Command | Update installed. Records before/after driver version.

packages.name: Network Fix - Driver Reinstall (ON-DEMAND ONLY)
packages.description: Removes and re-detects the Wi-Fi adapter, reinstalling its driver from the local driver store. Exports and restores the active WLAN profile, and arms a boot watchdog before touching the device.
packages.notes: Highest-risk package in the kit - the only one that can strand a remote device. Do not assign to a group. Detection is a hard preflight and exits 1 only when every safety precondition passes; a 14-day per-device cooldown limits the blast radius of a mis-assignment.

packages.name: Network Fix - Stack Reset (ON-DEMAND ONLY)
packages.description: Winsock + IP stack reset. Requires a reboot to fully apply. Heavy hammer - last software step before the Stopping Rule.
packages.notes: Do not assign to a group. A 7-day per-device cooldown limits the blast radius of a mis-assignment.
